linear ODE for the function $y = y(x)$:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)\cdot y=\cos{\left(x \right)}$
Write the equation in the form $\frac{d}{dx}(yI(x)) = I(x)Q(x)$, where $I(x)$ is an integrating factor."] [:db/add "03037866-9e99-5a94-acdf-a5e7b89db4df" :question/worked-solution "This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+P(x)y=Q(x)
$$

with $P(x)=\frac{10}{3}$ and $Q(x)=\cos{\left(x \right)}.$ We proceed to find an integrating factor $I(x)$ using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,dx} \\  & =e^{\int \left(\frac{10}{3}\right)\,dx} \\  & =e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply our differential equation through by $I(x)=e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\frac{dy}{dx}+\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)\cdot y\right) & =\left(e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(x \right)}\right) \\ \left(e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \frac{dy}{dx}+\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)\cdot \left(e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\right)\cdot y & =\left(e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(x \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the left hand side as $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y\cdot I(x)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}\left(y\cdot \left(e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\right)\right) & =\left(e^{\frac{10 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(x \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "03037866-9e99-5a94-acdf-a5e7b89db4df" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "03037866-9e99-5a94-acdf-a5e7b89db4df" :question/answer-fields linear ODE for the function $y=y(x):$

$$
\left(x\right)\cdot \frac{dy}{dx}-\left(x\right)\cdot y=x^{2}
$$

Write the equation in the form $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(yI(x))=I(x)Q(x),$ where $I(x)$ is an integrating factor.

Assume $x>0$."] [:db/add "1c8efe23-e1fe-5151-83ef-1ed23bccc20c" :question/worked-solution "First, we write the equation in standard form. This gives

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}-y=x.
$$

This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+P(x)y=Q(x)
$$

with $P(x)=-1$ and $Q(x)=x.$ We proceed to find an integrating factor $I(x)$ using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,dx} \\  & =e^{\int \left(-1\right)\,dx} \\  & =e^{- x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply our differential equation through by $I(x)=e^{- x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(e^{- x}\right)\cdot \left(\frac{dy}{dx}-y\right) & =\left(e^{- x}\right)\cdot \left(x\right) \\ \left(e^{- x}\right)\cdot \frac{dy}{dx}-\left(1\right)\cdot \left(e^{- x}\right)\cdot y & =\left(e^{- x}\right)\cdot \left(x\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the left hand side as $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y\cdot I(x)):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}\left(y\cdot \left(e^{- x}\right)\right) & =\left(e^{- x}\right)\cdot \left(x\right)\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "1c8efe23-e1fe-5151-83ef-1ed23bccc20c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "1c8efe23-e1fe-5151-83ef-1ed23bccc20c" :question/answer-fields
